lines: Specialisation can be seen as a response to the problem of an increasing accumulation of scientific knowledge. By splitting up the subject matter into smaller units, one man could continue to handle the information and use it as the basis for further research. But specialisation was only one of a series of related developments in science affecting the process of communication. Another was the growing **professionalisation** of scientific activity.
专业分工可以被看作是对科学知识不断累积这一问题所作出的回应。通过把学科细分为更小的单元，个人就能继续处理这些信息，并以此作为进一步研究的基础。但专业分工只是科学领域一系列影响交流过程的相关发展中的一个。另一个发展则是科学活动的日益职业化。

lines: No clear-cut distinction can be drawn between professionals and amateurs in science: exceptions can be found to any rule. Nevertheless, the word "**amateur**" does carry a connotation that the person concerned is not fully integrated into the scientific community and, in particular, may not fully share its values. The growth of specialisation in the nineteenth century, with its consequent requirement of a longer, more complex training, implied greater problems for amateur participation in science. The trend was naturally most obvious in those areas of science based especially on a mathematical or laboratory training, and can be illustrated in terms of the development of geology in the United Kingdom.
在科学领域，专业人员与业余人员之间无法划出泾渭分明的界线：任何规则都有例外。不过，“业余”一词的确含有这样的意味：相关人员没有完全融入科学界，尤其是可能不完全认同这个群体的价值观念。十九世纪专业化的成长，以及随之而来的对更长时、更复杂训练的要求，意味着业余人员参与科学活动遇到了更大的障碍。这一趋势在那些特别依赖数学或实验室训练的学科中自然最为明显，英国地质学的发展便可以用来说明这一点。

lines: A comparison of British geological publications over the last century and a half reveals not simply an increasing emphasis on the primacy of research, but also a changing definition of what constitutes an acceptable research paper. Thus, in the nineteenth century, local geological studies represented worthwhile research in their own right; but, in the twentieth century, local studies have increasingly become acceptable to professionals only if they incorporate, and reflect on, the wider geological picture. Amateurs, on the other hand, have continued to pursue local studies in the old way. The overall result has been to make entrance to professional geological journals harder for amateurs, a result that has been reinforced by the widespread introduction of refereeing, first by national journals in the nineteenth century and then by several local geological journals in the twentieth century. As a logical consequence of this development, separate journals have now appeared aimed mainly towards either professional or amateur readership. A rather similar process of differentiation has led to professional geologists coming together nationally within one or two specific societies, whereas the amateurs have tended either to remain in local societies or to come together nationally in a different way.

对过去一个半世纪英国地质学刊物的比较表明，不仅人们对研究首要地位的强调在不断加强，而且对“什么样的论文才算合格的研究成果”的界定也在变化。因此，在十九世纪，地方地质学研究本身就代表着有价值的科研工作；而到了二十世纪，地方研究只有融入并反思更广阔的地质图景，才会日益被专业人员所接受。另一方面，业余人员却继续沿用老一套的方式从事地方研究。其总的结果是，业余人员更难在专业地质学刊物上发表文章，而审稿制度的广泛推行又强化了这一结果——这种制度先是在十九世纪由国家级刊物引入，随后又在二十世纪进入几家地方地质刊物。这一发展的一个必然结果是，如今出现了分别主要面向专业读者或业余读者的不同刊物。另一个十分相似的分化过程，使得专业地质学家在全国范围内组成了一两个专门的学会，而业余人员则往往要么留在地方学会，要么以另一种方式组成全国性团体。

lines: A great deal of attention is being paid today to the so-called digital divide -- the division of the world into the info (information) rich and the info poor. And that divide does exist today. My wife and I lectured about this looming danger twenty years ago. What was less visible then, however, were the new, positive forces that work against the digital divide. There are reasons to be optimistic.
如今，人们十分关注所谓的数字鸿沟问题——即世界被分为信息富有者和信息贫穷者。这一鸿沟在今天确实存在。二十年前，我和妻子就曾就这一迫近的危险发表演讲。但当时还不太显眼的，是一些正在对抗数字鸿沟的新的积极力量。我们有理由保持乐观。

lines: There are **technological** reasons to hope the digital divide will narrow. As the Internet becomes more and more commercialized, it is in the interest of business to universalize access -- after all, the more people online, the more potential customers there are. More and more governments, afraid their countries will be left behind, want to spread Internet access. Within the next decade or two, one to two billion people on the planet will be netted together. As a result, I now believe the digital divide will narrow rather than widen in the years ahead. And that is very good news because the Internet may well be the most powerful tool for **combating** world poverty that we've ever had.
从技术层面看，我们有理由希望数字鸿沟将会缩小。随着互联网日益商业化，普及上网符合商界的利益——毕竟，上网的人越多，潜在的客户就越多。越来越多的政府担心自己的国家会落后于人，也想推广互联网。在今后一二十年内，地球上将有十亿到二十亿人被网络连接在一起。因此，我现在相信，数字鸿沟在未来的岁月里将会缩小而不是扩大。这是非常好的消息，因为互联网很可能是我们迄今拥有的对抗世界贫困的最有力工具。

lines: To take advantage of this tool, some impoverished countries will have to get over their outdated anti-colonial **prejudices** with respect to foreign investment. Countries that still think foreign investment is an invasion of their sovereignty might well study the history of infrastructure (the basic structural foundations of a society) in the United States. When the United States built its industrial infrastructure, it didn't have the capital to do so. And that is why America's Second Wave infrastructure -- including roads, harbors, highways, ports and so on -- were built with foreign investment. The English, the Germans, the Dutch and the French were investing in Britain's former colony. They financed them. Immigrant Americans built them. Guess who owns them now? The Americans. I believe the same thing would be true in places like Brazil or anywhere else for that matter. The more foreign capital you have helping you build your Third Wave infrastructure, which today is an electronic infrastructure, the better off you're going to be. That doesn't mean lying down and becoming fooled, or letting foreign corporations run uncontrolled. But it does mean recognizing how important they can be in building the energy and telecom **infrastructures** needed to take full advantage of the Internet.

要利用好这一工具，一些贫困国家就必须摈弃它们在外国投资问题上过时的反殖民偏见。那些仍把外国投资视为主权入侵的国家，不妨研究一下美国基础设施建设（社会的基本结构基础）的历史。美国修建工业基础设施时，没有所需的资金。正因如此，美国的第二次浪潮基础设施——包括道路、海港、公路、码头等等——都是利用外资建成的。英国人、德国人、荷兰人和法国人都在这个英国的前殖民地投资。他们提供了建设资金。移民美国的人们负责建造。猜猜现在谁拥有它们？美国人。我相信，在巴西或其他任何地方，情况都会同样如此。帮助建设第三次浪潮基础设施（即当今的电子基础设施）的外国资本越多，你就会越富裕。这并不意味着任人摆布、上当受骗，也不是让外国公司不受约束地经营。但这确实意味着要认识到：在建设充分利用互联网所必需的能源和电信基础设施方面，它们能发挥多么重要的作用。

lines: This is an explosive situation for any industry, particularly a declining one. Here is a troubled business that keeps hiring employees whose attitudes vastly annoy the customers. Then it sponsors lots of symposiums and a credibility project dedicated to wondering why customers are annoyed and fleeing in large numbers. If it did, it would open up its diversity program, now focused narrowly on race and gender, and look for reporters who differ broadly by outlook, values, education, and class.

lines: There's no question that the big are getting bigger and more powerful. Multinational corporations accounted for less than 20% of international trade in 1982. Today the figure is more than 25% and growing rapidly. International affiliates account for a fast-growing segment of production in economies that open up and welcome foreign investment. In Argentina, for instance, after the reforms of the early 1990s, multinationals went from 43% to almost 70% of the industrial production of the 200 largest firms. This phenomenon has created serious concerns over the role of smaller economic firms, of national businessmen and over the ultimate stability of the world economy.

毫无疑问，大企业正变得越来越庞大、越来越强势。1982年，跨国公司在国际贸易中所占的比重还不到20%。如今，这一比例已超过25%，而且还在迅速上升。在那些对外开放、欢迎外国投资的经济体中，跨国公司的国际分支机构在生产中所占的份额也在迅速增长。例如，在阿根廷，20世纪90年代初的改革之后，跨国公司在200家最大企业工业产值中所占的份额，从43%上升到了近70%。这一现象使人们对规模较小的企业和本国商人所发挥的作用，以及世界经济最终的稳定性，产生了严重的担忧。

lines: When I decided to quit my full-time employment it never occurred to me that I might become a part of a new international trend. A lateral move that hurt my pride and blocked my professional progress prompted me to abandon my relatively high profile career although, in the manner of a disgraced government minister, I covered my exit by claiming "I wanted to spend more time with my family".

lines: Curiously, some two-and-a-half years and two novels later, my experiment in what the Americans term "**downshifting**" has turned my tired excuse into an absolute reality. I have been transformed from a passionate advocate of the philosophy of "having it all", preached by Linda Kelsey for the past seven years in the pages of She magazine, into a woman who is happy to settle for a bit of everything.
奇怪的是，在经历了大约两年半的时间并写了两部小说之后，我这个被美国人称为“放慢生活节奏”的尝试，已使我那老掉牙的借口变成了不折不扣的现实。我已经从一个“样样都要”哲学的热烈鼓吹者——琳达·凯尔西过去七年里一直在《她》杂志上宣扬这种哲学——变成了一个知足常乐、随遇而安的女人。

lines: Through his research, Pearson is able to put dates to most of the breakthroughs that can be predicted. However, there are still no forecasts for when faster-than-light travel will be available, or when human cloning will be perfected, or when time travel will be possible. But he does expect social problems as a result of technological advances. A boom in neighborhood surveillance cameras will, for example, cause problems in 2010, while the arrival of synthetic lifelike robots will mean people may not be able to distinguish between their human friends and the droids.
通过研究，皮尔逊能够为大多数可以预测的突破确定日期。然而，对于超光速旅行何时可以实现、人类克隆何时臻于完善、时间旅行何时成为可能，目前尚无预测。但他确实预计技术进步会带来社会问题。例如，住宅区监控摄像机的激增将在2010年引发种种问题，而合成仿真机器人的出现则意味着人们可能无法分辨人类朋友和机器人。

data.title: Love（46题，图片：一盏油灯在黑暗中发光，寓意'爱心是一盏灯，在越黑暗的地方越明亮'）
data.directions_en: Among all the worthy feelings of mankind, love is probably the noblest, but everyone has his/her own understanding of it. There has been a discussion recently on the issue in a newspaper. Write an essay to the newspaper to 1) show your understanding of the symbolic meaning of the picture below, 2) give a specific example, and 3) give your suggestion as to the best way to show love. You should write about 200 words on ANSWER SHEET 2. (20 points)
data.directions_zh: 在人类所有可贵的情感中，爱也许是最高尚的，但每个人对爱都有自己的理解。最近，一家报纸围绕这个问题展开了讨论。请为该报写一篇文章，内容包括：1）说明你对下图象征意义的理解；2）给出一个具体例子；3）就表达爱的最佳方式提出建议。应在答题卡2上写约200词。（20分）
sample: Among all the worthy feelings of mankind, love is probably the noblest. The picture shows a small oil lamp giving off bright light in complete darkness, which symbolizes a profound truth: love is like a lamp -- the darker the place is, the brighter it shines.
在人类一切美好的情感之中，爱心也许是最崇高的。图画描绘了一盏油灯在一片漆黑中散发明亮的光芒，这蕴含着一个深刻的道理：爱心犹如一盏灯——越是黑暗的地方，它照得越亮。

sample: A specific example makes this point clear. During the 1998 floods in China, millions of people in the flooded areas lost their homes overnight. Warm-hearted people from all walks of life donated money, clothes and food, and PLA soldiers risked their lives to rescue those trapped in the water. It was precisely in that darkest hour that the lamp of love shone most brilliantly, giving the flood victims hope and courage to rebuild their homes.
一个具体的例子可以说明这一点。1998年中国发生特大洪水时，数百万灾区群众一夜之间流离失所。社会各界的热心人士纷纷捐款捐物，解放军战士更是冒着生命危险营救被洪水围困的群众。恰恰是在那最黑暗的时刻，爱心的灯光闪耀得最为明亮，给了灾民重建家园的希望和勇气。

sample: In my opinion, the best way to show love is not merely to make grand promises, but to offer timely help to those who need it most. Whether it is a small donation, a word of comfort or a helping hand, as long as we bring light to the darkest corners of the world, love will be passed on from heart to heart, and our society will become warmer and more harmonious.
